title: Multimodal Remote Sensing Change Detection: An Image Matching Perspective
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: An unsupervised multimodal change-detection framework using local template matching, response-peak offsets, robust registration residuals and CRF structural relationships.

verification.notes: The local BRIGHT transfer code is a controlled translation-only probe, not a full reproduction.

title: Superpixel Sampling Networks
abstract: A differentiable SLIC-style network that learns task-specific superpixels with iterative pixel-superpixel association updates.
source: official paper and NVIDIA code repository

verification.notes: Official code is Caffe-era and should be used as algorithmic reference rather than copied verbatim.

title: Retrieval Augmented Classification for Long-Tail Visual Recognition
abstract: A base image encoder is augmented with a parallel retrieval branch over an external memory for long-tail recognition.

verification.notes: Supports a parallel memory branch, not hard replacement of the base classifier.

title: Tip-Adapter: Training-Free Adaption of CLIP for Few-Shot Classification
abstract: A key-value cache constructed from few-shot training samples supplies residual evidence to a frozen CLIP classifier.

verification.notes: The cache is effective because its key space is already strongly pretrained; this assumption is not satisfied by the current P3 region key.

title: RIFT: Multi-Modal Image Matching Based on Radiation-Variation Insensitive Feature Transform
abstract: Phase-congruency detection and maximum-index-map descriptors improve matching under nonlinear radiometric differences across modalities.

verification.notes: Useful fallback descriptor if frozen neural features fail the matching audit.

title: BRIGHT: A Globally Distributed Multimodal Building Damage Assessment Dataset with Very-High-Resolution for All-Weather Disaster Response
abstract: A globally distributed pre-event optical and post-event SAR benchmark for building damage assessment across 14 disaster events.
source: official ESSD paper and BRIGHT repository

verification.notes: Event-level robustness is a first-class evaluation requirement.
